name: AD Module Enumeration (Microsoft ActiveDirectory Module)
description: Use the built-in Microsoft AD PowerShell module for LDAP-based enumeration. Stealthier than PowerView — uses legitimate AD admin tooling.
notes: AD module is pre-installed on DCs and RSAT machines. Load on regular machines: Import-Module ActiveDirectory

defense.why_it_works: The Microsoft ActiveDirectory PowerShell module communicates with DCs via LDAP/ADWS (port 9389) using the authenticated user's credentials. It is a signed Microsoft DLL — bypasses application allowlisting. Get-ADDomain, Get-ADUser, Get-ADGroup, Get-ADComputer return rich AD object data without elevated privileges.
defense.prerequisites: Domain user account. RSAT installed or AD module imported from DC. PowerShell execution. LDAP/ADWS access (ports 389/636/9389).
defense.impact: T1482 Domain Trust Discovery + T1069.002 Permission Groups Discovery + T1087.002 Account Discovery. Maps the full AD structure: users, groups, OUs, trusts, computers, GPOs — foundational data for attack path planning.
defense.detection:
LDAP/ADWS queries from workstations (port 9389) — unusual for non-admins. Event 4662 for AD object access. MDI 'LDAP reconnaissance' alert. PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event 4104): Import-Module ActiveDirectory or Get-AD* commands.
Adversary uses nltest, PowerShell, or Win32/.NET API to enumerate domain trust relationships (via DSEnumerateDomainTrusts, GetAllTrustRelationships, or LDAP queries), followed by discovery or authentication staging (DET0007/AN0016).
Detection of adversary enumeration of domain or local group memberships via native tools such as net.exe, PowerShell, or WMI; may precede lateral movement or privilege escalation (DET0179/AN0507).
Group enumeration using 'id', 'groups', or 'getent group' commands on Linux, often followed by privilege escalation or SSH lateral movement (AN0508).
Group membership checks via 'dscl', 'dscacheutil', or 'id' on macOS, executed via terminal or automation scripts (AN0509).
defense.artifacts: Event 4104: Import-Module ActiveDirectory + Get-AD* | DC Event 4662: LDAP reads from workstation | MDI: LDAP reconnaissance alert | ADWS port 9389 connections in netflow | Zeek ldap.log: bulk query from non-admin
defense.prevention:
PowerShell Constrained Language Mode (CLM) via WDAC/AppLocker. Script Block Logging + Module Logging (GPO). MDI deployment. Restrict LDAP/ADWS ports to admin hosts only.
Audit: Map the trusts within existing domains/forests and keep trust relationships to a minimum.
Network Segmentation: Employ network segmentation for sensitive domains.
This technique cannot be easily mitigated with preventive controls since it is based on the abuse of system features.
Operating System Configuration: Prevent administrator account enumeration via UAC (GPO: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators).
User Account Management: Manage creation, modification, use, and permissions associated with user accounts.
defense.evasion: Use ADSI (.NET System.DirectoryServices) directly instead of AD module — same queries, different process signature. Query from a legitimate IT workstation. Use -Filter with small OUs to avoid volume anomalies.
defense.misconfiguration: All domain users can read most AD object attributes by default. No Script Block Logging. No CLM enforcement. MDI not deployed. No LDAP-tier restriction.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# PowerShell execution unrestricted:
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List  # All scopes: Unrestricted or RemoteSigned

# No Script Block Logging:
# HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging
# EnableScriptBlockLogging = 0

# ADWS port 9389 accessible from all workstations
defense.secure_config:
# Enable Script Block Logging via GPO:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging' -Name EnableScriptBlockLogging -Value 1

# CLM via WDAC (AllowMicrosoft base policy):
# Unsigned scripts → Constrained Language Mode

# MDI: built-in LDAP reconnaissance detection

# Tiering: block workstations from DC LDAP/ADWS ports at firewall:
# deny tcp 10.0.1.0/24 (workstations) 10.0.0.10/32 (DC) eq 389,636,9389
